Jules (AE): Heads-up: prospect Neon wants explicit price-protection and MFN. They want it to apply to any future list price changes for the same SKU for 12 months.
Sam (Solutions): That could be interpreted to include list price reductions for product packaging changes.
Jordan (Legal): Their draft: "Customer shall be entitled to any more favorable prices Redwood offers to any other customer for substantially the same services during the Term." No carveouts.
Priya (Deal Desk): Typical pushback is to ask for carveouts and a nonprecedent clause. Also we need approval for any POC concession.
Marta (CFO): If we give POC or pilot discounts, we must ensure it doesn't reset the baseline pricing for other customers.
Jules (AE): Neon asked for 60% off for a 30-day POC. They may try to argue that's the market price.
Jordan (Legal): Recommend redline: exclude time-limited promos <=30 days, partner/channel programs, and explicitly exclude one-off concessions documented in the SOW. Add a liability cap for retro credits equal to 3 months of fees.
Sam (Solutions): Can we label the POC discount as a "pilot concession" and include explicit non-MFN language in the SOW?
Priya (Deal Desk): Yes, but Deal Desk needs to log the concession to avoid accidental recurrence.
Marta (CFO): Approve the pilot concession only if: (1) non-MFN clause, (2) cap = 3 months OR $150k whichever is lower, (3) minimum annualized commit after pilot >= $120k.
Jordan (Legal): I'll include sample language and send back a redline.
DealDeskBot: Created DD-5012 for Neon: Pilot concession request logged.
Jules (AE): Thanks. I'll negotiate with the buyer to accept carveouts.
Sam (Solutions): And I'll flag Product - buyers sometimes try to extend MFN to priority roadmap features.
Priya (Deal Desk): Noted. We'll require feature parity carveout.
Jordan (Legal): Drafting now.
Marta (CFO): If they insist on uncarved MFN or unlimited retro credits, we walk.
Jules (AE): Copy that.
